spec.title: State the trigger and the medium for Phase 4 worktree isolation
spec.problem: commands/pipeline.md dispatches all Phase 4 panelists into ONE worktree (the dispatch worktree named in the shared preamble). Read-only review is fine there, but several lenses legitimately run leave-one-out mutation batteries that edit a tracked file in place and restore it, and four reviewers collided in a single #17 panel: QA measured three preset rows as dead cells and watched a glob count move 14 to 15 with no checkout of its own; SecOps observed a surface module losing a glob row on two observations and rated it HIGH because a `git commit -a` during a fix round would ship a narrowed halting control; DBA and Dev both saw the file transiently dirty and correctly declined to `git checkout --` it, which is the battery's own restore mechanism, so isolation-less sharing also DISARMS the safe restore. Three later confirmations: a concurrent process modified commands/pipeline.md mid-run inside this worktree during #21 Phase 2 and self-restored inside roughly a minute with zero forensic trace; DevOps REVOKED its own before/after bracket remedy because the event began and ended inside one run window, so two boundary snapshots cannot distinguish 'never contaminated' from 'contaminated and the window closed between checks'; and at least five run.sh processes ran concurrently in this one checkout during #21 Phase 4. Two SEPARATE harms are tangled here and the issue's three options are presented as alternatives to one harm: (H1) corrupted MEASUREMENTS, which only isolation prevents and which no boundary check can even detect; and (H2) a planted mutation SHIPPING via a blanket `git commit -a` in a fix round, which is a point event and which explicit-path staging INSTRUCTS AGAINST but does not prevent. Underneath both sits a third defect the issue does not name: nine agent contracts already assert that a mutating reviewer needs worktree isolation while naming no TRIGGER and no MEDIUM, and the issue's own option (b), 'mutation work on a copy in a tmp dir', names a medium that is measurably WRONG. Phase 2 round 1 added a fourth: the OBVIOUS medium rule ('use a git-complete checkout') is ALSO wrong, because a tar/cp copy of a LINKED worktree carries its `.git` FILE verbatim and therefore ALIASES the dispatch worktree's gitdir, index, HEAD and branch, measuring identically to correct isolation while a `git commit -a` inside it commits the dispatch worktree. Phase 2 round 2 added a fifth, and it is the one that decides the shipped spelling: the outcome check itself is topology-dependent. `git rev-parse --git-dir` prints a RELATIVE `.git` in a main checkout and an ABSOLUTE path in a linked worktree, so in a main-checkout dispatch the predicate falsely REFUSES a real `git clone --no-hardlinks` and falsely ADMITS a plain SUBDIRECTORY of the dispatch checkout, which shares the dispatch index, HEAD and branch. The rule has to be stated as an OUTCOME a reader checks, in a spelling that resolves the same way in every topology.
spec.root_cause: The isolation rule was written as a conclusion ('mutating reviewers need worktree isolation') without the two things that make a rule executable: WHEN it fires (any tracked-file write during Phase 4, which no contract says) and WHAT the isolated tree must BE (a tree with its OWN gitdir and a working index, which no contract says). The shared-worktree dispatch in the Phase 4 preamble is then the default that fills the gap. The medium half has three failure modes, all measured: a copy with NO git (`tar --exclude .git`) breaks the suites that diagnose their own source root through git, so they read falsely red (83/2 against 85/0 on identical bytes); a copy WITH the linked worktree's `.git` file intact resolves to the SOURCE gitdir, so it reads perfectly green while sharing the index it is supposed to be isolated from; and the naive spelling of the outcome check, `rev-parse --git-dir`, compares a RELATIVE string against an ABSOLUTE one whenever the dispatch tree is a main checkout, which admits a bare subdirectory of that same checkout. All three are refused by comparing ABSOLUTE gitdirs (`rev-parse --absolute-git-dir`) and requiring `git ls-files` to succeed with a non-zero count.
requirements: R1. State in the Phase 4 preamble that the DISPATCH worktree is READ-ONLY to panelists: no panelist writes to a tracked file there, at any tier, on a full round or a delta round. Name both harms distinctly (a corrupted measurement, and a `git commit -a` shipping a narrowed halting control) so a reader cannot collapse them into one. In the SAME passage, state that a panelist who says nothing about tracked writes has said NOTHING: the read-only declaration must not turn silence into an implied claim of compliance. That sentence ships in the preamble AND in all nine agent contracts, because the panelist who could make the claim meets only the contract and the prompt, never a schema.

R2. Fix the MEDIUM in the nine agent contracts and in the Phase 4 preamble by stating the OUTCOME a reader checks, not the tool: an isolated tree qualifies only when `git -C <isolated> rev-parse --absolute-git-dir` DIFFERS from `git -C <dispatch> rev-parse --absolute-git-dir` AND `git -C <isolated> ls-files` EXITS 0 with a non-zero count. Both clauses, in that direction, and in that SPELLING. `--absolute-git-dir` is load-bearing and not a stylistic choice: `--git-dir` prints a relative `.git` in a main checkout and an absolute path in a linked worktree, so the same predicate returns different verdicts on the same tree shape depending on the dispatch topology (measured, four cells, below). Do NOT 'harden' the compared field to `--git-common-dir`: two linked worktrees of one repo SHARE a common dir, so a common-dir comparison would refuse `git worktree add --detach`, the primary mechanism this rule recommends. State that clause 1 is meaningful only when `rev-parse` EXITS 0, so a reader cannot record clause 1 as satisfied on a git-less copy where rev-parse fails and stdout is empty. Name `git worktree add --detach <REVIEWED_SHA>` and `git clone --no-hardlinks` as two mechanisms that satisfy the check in EVERY topology, and `cp`/`tar`/`rsync`/editor copy as mechanisms this rule does not admit - but state WHY as a fact rather than as a prediction the check will not honour, because what the check SAYS about a copy is topology-conditional and a flat 'copies are refused' is measured-false: where the dispatch tree is a linked worktree its `.git` is a FILE, a copy preserving it resolves to the dispatch gitdir and is REFUSED; where the dispatch tree is a main checkout its `.git` is a DIRECTORY, the same copy is an independent repository and is ADMITTED. That instability is itself the argument for using git rather than a copy, since the copier cannot tell which case it is in from inside the copy. The check is what binds. Carry the measurement that forces this (the five cells below), not the conclusion alone.

R3. State the TRIGGER: isolation is owed by any panelist ABOUT TO WRITE A TRACKED FILE, not by the panel as a whole. Reviewers that only read stay in the dispatch worktree. The trigger ships in all nine agent contracts and in the Phase 4 preamble, and AC6 is the criterion that fails on its omission.

R4. Place the isolated tree OUTSIDE the repository root AND somewhere no other local user can read it, and name its removal as the obligation of the agent that created it IN THE SAME SENTENCE that authorises creating it. The privacy half is an OUTCOME, not a location allowlist: the tree's contents must be unreachable by another local user, which holds when some component of the path from the filesystem root to the tree denies group and other traversal, or when the tree itself denies group and other read. State the ways to meet it and the live way to miss it, both measured. In that same passage state the residual honestly: removal is unenforceable on an agent that is cut off (the same interruption the isolation rule exists for), `git worktree prune` reclaims a registration only after its DIRECTORY is gone, no actor in this pipeline sweeps, and the informal version of this convention has a measured compliance record of zero. Do not claim removal is enforced; what this change buys is ATTRIBUTABILITY.

R5. Hold ARTIFACT_DIR EXACTLY where it is: shards continue to go to the single absolute artifact dir in the dispatch worktree, and the preamble says so explicitly, because the naive reading of isolation is to write the shard beside the isolated tree, and that is the string a frozen suite forbids and the topology the out-of-scope merge and sync steps assume.

R6. Bind Phase 4 COMMIT hygiene, and state its effect at the strength it actually has: before any Phase 4 fix commit, read and record `git status --porcelain`, stage explicit paths only, and never `git commit -a`, `git add -A` or `git add .`. The sentence that states R6's effect must say IN ITSELF both that this is the only one of the three legs sited at the ship event AND that nothing mechanically enforces it. No artifact sentence may say staging 'prevents' the shipping harm; it instructs against it. The rule ships in all nine agent contracts and in the Phase 4 preamble, because under an APPROVE_WITH_NOTES verdict the fix commit is plausibly the orchestrator's or Dev's rather than a panelist's, and a rule stated only in the agent contracts would miss the actor that fires it. AC7 is the criterion that fails on its omission and AC14 is the one that fails on a vacuous statement of it.

R7. Say in the preamble what a boundary check cannot do: a before/after `git status` pair is not evidence that a measurement taken in a shared tree was uncontaminated, because a contamination that opens and closes inside the window is invisible to both endpoints. Where isolation is declined and a measurement is taken in the shared tree anyway, require continuous sampling at a cadence under the observed cycle with the SAMPLES recorded, not a conclusion.

R9. Deliver the medium (R2), the trigger (R3) and the commit-hygiene rule (R6) to ALL NINE agent contracts, the population being the DIRECTORY LISTING of plugins/pipeline/agents/*.md and not a grep for any existing sentence. qa.md is in the delivered set: it states the isolation conclusion in its own words at qa.md:103 and is invisible to the literal grep that finds the other eight. Every edit stays outside the digest-frozen replicated span so its sha1 is unchanged. (Numbering preserved from round 2. R8, the `tracked_writes` schema attestation, is DELETED from this change and deferred to #76; see out_of_scope and the #76 row in measured_state.)
acceptance_criteria: AC1. In commands/pipeline.md, `grep -c 'write the shard beside your own worktree at <WORKTREE_PATH>/.pipeline/<issue>/'` is still 0 and `grep -c 'fallback-shards/peer-review.<role>.json'` is still exactly 1, so the two counts test-pipeline-telemetry.sh:91 and :93 pin are unmoved by the new prose.

AC2. The ten-copy replicated span still hashes to 14b65c48479dfceefb780689adccfbd53656b21e in all ten files, one hash for all ten, extracted from the `## The property, not the fix` line through the `This block is replicated verbatim in ten files.` line inclusive (15 lines). Extraction is by CONTENT anchor, never by line number, because this change renumbers the file. A handful of groups, or ten agreeing hashes that are not this one, means the extraction bounds were wrong, not that the block drifted. THE TERMINATOR ANCHOR MUST STAY UNIQUE, and this change is the first thing that could break it: the phrase `replicated verbatim` occurs EXACTLY ONCE in each of the ten files today (measured, 1/1 in all ten), and it is what the sed extraction stops on, so the new nine-copy block's closing sentence must read `copied byte-for-byte into all nine agent contracts` and must NEVER say `replicated verbatim`. Verified as a count, not a reading: post-change `grep -c 'replicated verbatim'` is still exactly 1 in each of the ten files, and `grep -c 'copied byte-for-byte'` over the nine agent contracts is 9 (pre-change count 0, measured). A second occurrence of `replicated verbatim` in any file is a new false-drift surface for AC2's own extraction and fails this criterion even if every digest still agrees.

AC3. `bash plugins/pipeline/tests/run.sh </dev/null` produces the same suite-by-suite pass/fail table as the pre-change baseline taken at the same SHA (34/34 suites green, test-config-doctor-surfaces.sh 85/0, test-pipeline-telemetry.sh 107/0), with no suite moving in either direction; the comparison is per suite, not on totals, and both runs are taken in a checkout no sibling process can write to.
AC4. The Phase 4 preamble states the read-only-dispatch-worktree rule and names the two harms as separate harms, with the boundary-check limitation stated as a limitation rather than as a remedy.

AC5. All NINE files in `plugins/pipeline/agents/*.md` carry the MEDIUM rule. Verified as a THREE-WAY equality over one literal chosen by the implementer and recorded in the impl-report: `ls plugins/pipeline/agents/*.md | wc -l` == `grep -rl '<medium literal>' plugins/pipeline/agents/*.md | wc -l` == 9. The impl-report ALSO records that literal's occurrence count over the same nine files in the PRE-change tree, and that count is 0, so the mandatory red below is attributable to the new rule's absence rather than to a pre-existing string. Measured disqualifications the implementer may not pick, because each already reads 9 or 3 pre-change and would make the criterion pass with the rule delivered to zero files: `worktree` 9/9, `git commit -a` 9/9, `porcelain` 3/9; `worktree isolation` reads 8/9 and would redden for the WRONG reason (qa.md's pre-existing wording, the exact 8-vs-9 confusion this criterion was rewritten to escape). The population is the directory listing, never a grep for the pre-existing isolation sentence. Demonstrated red by reverting qa.md ALONE to a form lacking the medium rule and running the check in that state (9 == 8), and by the degenerate case (0 == 9), so the equality is not satisfiable by two zeros.

AC6. All NINE agent contracts AND the Phase 4 preamble carry the TRIGGER: isolation is owed by a panelist about to write a tracked file, not by the panel as a whole. Verified as a SECOND three-way equality over a SECOND implementer-chosen literal, distinct from AC5's, recorded in the impl-report with its PRE-change occurrence count over the nine files, which must be 0: `ls plugins/pipeline/agents/*.md | wc -l` == `grep -rl '<trigger literal>' plugins/pipeline/agents/*.md | wc -l` == 9, AND `grep -c '<trigger literal>' plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md` >= 1. The literal must sit inside a sentence that names the writing act as the thing that fires the obligation and says read-only reviewers stay in the dispatch worktree. Demonstrated red THREE ways, each run separately: delete the trigger sentence from qa.md alone (9 == 8), delete it from the preamble alone (pipeline.md count 0), and the degenerate case where it is absent everywhere (0 == 9 and 0). Omitting R3 entirely must therefore fail this criterion on a count a reader takes from the diff alone.

AC7. All NINE agent contracts AND the Phase 4 preamble carry the COMMIT-HYGIENE rule. Verified as a THIRD three-way equality over a THIRD implementer-chosen literal, distinct from AC5's and AC6's, recorded in the impl-report with its PRE-change occurrence count over the nine files, which must be 0: `ls plugins/pipeline/agents/*.md | wc -l` == `grep -rl '<hygiene literal>' plugins/pipeline/agents/*.md | wc -l` == 9, AND `grep -c '<hygiene literal>' plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md` >= 1. The literal must sit inside a sentence that forbids `git commit -a`, `git add -A` and `git add .` before a Phase 4 fix commit and requires a recorded `git status --porcelain` read with explicit-path staging. MEASURED TRAP, stated so the implementer cannot walk into it: the literal may NOT itself be `git commit -a`, which already occurs in 9 of 9 agent files, nor `porcelain`, which occurs in 3 of 9; either would read GREEN with the rule delivered to zero files, which is precisely the failure SecOps measured for `worktree` against AC5. Demonstrated red by deleting the sentence from qa.md alone, from the preamble alone, and everywhere.

AC8. The medium rule is stated as an outcome check a reader RUNS, with both clauses and in this direction: the isolated tree's `git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir` DIFFERS from the dispatch worktree's, AND `git -C <isolated> ls-files` EXITS 0 with a non-zero count; and the text says clause 1 is meaningful only when `rev-parse` EXITS 0, so a git-less copy cannot be recorded as passing half a check it fails entirely. It carries a re-derivable observation naming the copy shape precisely: a `tar --exclude .git` copy (no git at all) reads 83/2 on test-config-doctor-surfaces.sh against 85/0 in the dispatch worktree, while a tar copy that PRESERVES the `.git` file reads 85/0 and reports a git-dir IDENTICAL to the dispatch worktree's. A reader following the stated recipe lands on the stated numbers.

AC9. The shipped spelling is topology-independent, decided by the SAME five-cell observation run TWICE - once with the dispatch tree a MAIN CHECKOUT and once with it a LINKED WORKTREE - with all verdicts recorded in the impl-report as run, under each of `--absolute-git-dir` and `--git-dir`. BOTH runs are built from a THROWAWAY `git clone --no-hardlinks <repo> <scratch>/dispatch` used as the stand-in dispatch tree, so no cell registers against the real repository; the run records the real repo's `git worktree list | wc -l` and `git status --porcelain | wc -l` before and after and both are unchanged (measured 18 and 0). The linked-worktree run is manufactured the same way plus `git -C <scratch>/origin worktree add --detach <scratch>/dispatch`. THE TOPOLOGY OF EACH RUN IS ASSERTED BEFORE ANY CELL IS JUDGED, never assumed: `<dispatch>/.git` is a DIRECTORY in the main-checkout run and a FILE in the linked-worktree run. A run that cannot show that is not a run in the topology it claims. The five cells, built from the dispatch tree of each run: (1) `git worktree add --detach`; (2) `git clone --no-hardlinks`; (3) a TRACKED subdirectory of the dispatch checkout (`plugins/pipeline/scripts`, 15 tracked files); (4) a tar copy PRESERVING `.git`; (5) a `tar --exclude .git` copy. Cell 3 being TRACKED is mandatory and the run must prove it was: an UNTRACKED subdirectory is refused under `--git-dir` because `ls-files` returns 0, which hides the very bug cell 3 exists to expose, so the run records the untracked subdirectory as a named CONTROL and shows it refusing for that unrelated reason (measured in the main-checkout run: `REFUSE(ls-files exit 0 count 0)`, against cell 3's `ADMIT(n=15)`). A run whose cell 3 refuses under `--git-dir` has used an untracked directory and got the right answer for the wrong reason. EXPECTED VERDICTS UNDER `--absolute-git-dir`, cell 4's being TOPOLOGY-CONDITIONAL: the MAIN-CHECKOUT run produces ADMIT / ADMIT / REFUSE / ADMIT / REFUSE, and the LINKED-WORKTREE run produces ADMIT / ADMIT / REFUSE / REFUSE / REFUSE. Cell 4's split is a MECHANISM, not an exception, and the shipped prose must state the mechanism: where `.git` is a DIRECTORY the tar copy is an independent repository with its own gitdir, its own index and 132 tracked files, and nothing written in it can reach the dispatch tree, so REFUSING it would refuse correct work; where `.git` is a FILE the copy resolves to the dispatch tree's own gitdir and shares its index, HEAD and branch, so admitting it would admit the harm. The run PROVES that mechanism rather than asserting it, by comparing the INODE of `<absolute-git-dir>/index` in cell 4 against the dispatch tree's: DIFFERENT in the main-checkout run (measured 279516207 vs 279511802), IDENTICAL in the linked-worktree run (measured 279532648 for both). A run reporting cell 4 REFUSE under `--absolute-git-dir` in the main-checkout topology has mis-run the cell or built the wrong topology; it is not evidence about the spelling, and the pre-amendment AC9 that demanded exactly that verdict in exactly that topology was unsatisfiable. THE BITE, which is what SecOps's conditional VETO rests on and which needs BOTH runs: under `--git-dir` the MAIN-CHECKOUT run produces ADMIT / REFUSE / ADMIT / REFUSE / REFUSE and the criterion FAILS on cell 2 (a real `git clone --no-hardlinks` falsely REFUSED, because both trees print the relative `.git`) and on cell 3 (a tracked subdirectory of the dispatch checkout falsely ADMITTED, where `git commit -a` commits the dispatch tree), while the LINKED-WORKTREE run under `--git-dir` produces ADMIT / ADMIT / REFUSE / REFUSE / REFUSE, all five correct. That second row is ASSERTED, not incidental: `--git-dir` is indistinguishable from the right answer in the topology this pipeline actually dispatches into, which is why two review rounds passed it, so a criterion run only there cannot fail and the main-checkout run is the one that decides. AC9's pre-amendment prediction that `--git-dir` REFUSES cell 1 is WITHDRAWN as measured-false: it ADMITS, because a main checkout prints the relative `.git` while a linked worktree prints an absolute path, so the two strings differ by accident rather than by identity; cell 1 therefore does not discriminate the spelling in either topology under `--git-dir` and no verdict of this criterion may rest on it. `--git-common-dir` is refused on its own evidence: it FAILS cell 1 of the LINKED-WORKTREE run (REFUSE - two linked worktrees of one repo share a common dir, so it refuses `git worktree add --detach`, the primary mechanism R2 recommends) and FAILS cells 2 and 3 of the main-checkout run. `--absolute-git-dir` is therefore the ONLY spelling that produces the correct verdict in all ten cells across both topologies, and the criterion passes for it alone. Independently observable on the diff without running anything: `grep -c 'absolute-git-dir'` over the nine agent contracts is 9 and over commands/pipeline.md is >= 1, the count of `rev-parse --git-dir` USED AS THE ISOLATION PREDICATE is 0 in every changed file, `--git-common-dir` is not the compared field anywhere, and the shipped medium paragraph states cell 4's topology-conditionality with its `.git`-directory-versus-file mechanism, so a reader who copied a tree is told what the check will say about it and why.

AC10. `node plugins/pipeline/scripts/config-doctor.mjs --self-test` reports the same passed/failed counts as before the change, and the doctor's output against this repository still contains no occurrence of the literal WARNING (the assertion at test-config-doctor-surfaces.sh:386, which is out of scope to repair).

AC12. Every changed line in commands/pipeline.md lies either in the `### Risk-tiered orchestration depth` subsection or in the Phase 4 PREAMBLE span (from the `## Phase 4: Peer Review Panel (parallel)` heading to the line before the `### Dispatch model routing` heading), and NO changed line lies inside the digest-frozen span (the `## The property, not the fix` line through the `This block is replicated verbatim in ten files.` line inclusive). The resolver is FENCE-AWARE, toggling state on every ``` line and ignoring headings inside a fence. Its demonstration is anchored on CONTENT, never on line numbers, and is run ON THE POST-CHANGE FILE: the probe lines are the unique line containing `**Halves.**` (1 occurrence, inside the frozen span by construction) and the unique line containing `WRITE YOUR SHARD FIRST` (1 occurrence, inside the preamble fence and outside the frozen span). Both must resolve to `## Phase 4: Peer Review Panel (parallel)` under the fence-aware walk and to the phantom `## The property, not the fix` under a fence-blind `grep -n '^## '` walk, and that difference must be printed. The frozen-span exclusion is a SECOND, separate guard: the `**Halves.**` probe passes the section resolver and must be refused by the span check, while the `WRITE YOUR SHARD FIRST` probe passes both. Do NOT anchor on `Agent({subagent_type: "ba"`, which occurs TWICE in the file (measured) and is not a unique probe.

AC13. Silence-is-not-compliance is stated in BOTH places a reader meets the read-only rule, and each site is judged by its own observation, because the two sites serve two reader paths and a reader who meets one never sees the other: `grep -c '<disclosure literal>' plugins/pipeline/commands/pipeline.md` >= 1 AND `grep -rl '<disclosure literal>' plugins/pipeline/agents/*.md | wc -l` == 9, over one implementer-chosen literal recorded in the impl-report with its pre-change count of 0 over the nine files. Falsifiable by deleting the sentence from exactly ONE site and finding that site's own count reports absence while the other site is untouched. A criterion satisfied by either site alone would let the read-only declaration ship the inference 'nobody said they wrote anything, therefore nobody did' to whichever reader path was left uncovered.

AC14. R6's effect is stated at least once and never overstated, and the presence half is asserted FIRST and UNCONDITIONALLY so that stating nothing is a FAILURE rather than a vacuous pass: the count of AC7's hygiene literal over the changed files is >= 1 (unconditional), AND every sentence in the diff that states R6's effect carries, in that SAME sentence, both that this is the only one of the three legs sited at the ship event AND that nothing mechanically enforces it, AND no sentence anywhere in the diff or in this spec says explicit-path staging PREVENTS the shipping harm. The round-2 phrasing ('Wherever R6's effect is stated...') is deleted: it passed vacuously when R6's effect was stated nowhere, which is the same defect this issue exists to fix, one layer up.

AC15. The isolation passage records what an operator needs to attribute a leftover tree: it names the worktree's registry NAME (the `<name>` in `<git-common-dir>/worktrees/<name>`, which is what `git worktree prune -v` prints) as the identity to record, and states explicitly that removal is unenforceable on an interrupted agent, that no actor sweeps today, and that `git worktree prune` reclaims a registration only once its directory is gone. It does NOT claim an enforcement point that this scope has none for. The registry-name instruction survives the narrowing even though the typed home for it did not: the identity is now recorded in prose, in `notes` or in a free-form field, and the archive redactor's LEADING_SPAN rewrite (knowledge-store.mjs:147, applied at :195) still destroys a value that OPENS with an absolute path, so the passage must say the name and not the path.

AC16. R4's location clause states BOTH halves and refuses no correct work, demonstrated with one `stat` per case at the reviewed SHA: it REFUSES the live counter-example `/private/tmp/sketchB-43` (a registered detached worktree, drwxr-xr-x, whose whole ancestor chain `/private/tmp` drwxrwxrwt, `/private` drwxr-xr-x, `/` drwxr-xr-x grants other-traversal, so a full tracked-content checkout is readable by every local user); it REFUSES a bare `/private/tmp/<name>` created under the default umask 022 (drwxr-xr-x, measured); it ADMITS the session scratchpad tree, whose own mode is drwxr-xr-x but whose ancestor `/private/tmp/claude-501` is drwx------ so traversal is denied; and it ADMITS `$TMPDIR` (drwx------ measured). The clause must be an OUTCOME over the whole path, not a directory allowlist: `~/.cache` is drwxr-xr-x on this machine, so a tree created there under the default umask IS world-readable and must be refused, while the same tree created 0700 must be admitted. A clause phrased as 'a directory not readable by other local users', decided on the CONTAINING directory alone, gets `~/.cache` wrong in the admitting direction; a clause decided on the LEAF alone gets the session scratchpad wrong in the refusing direction. Both wrong spellings were measured; the criterion fails on either.

defect_fixed.what: The shipped location walk did not terminate on a path that does not exist. Shipped form: p=$(cd <the-tree> && pwd -P); while :; do ls -ld "$p"; [ "$p" = / ] && break; p=$(dirname "$p"); done. When the cd fails the assignment leaves p EMPTY; dirname "" is '.', dirname '.' is '.', so p never becomes '/' and the loop runs forever.

defect_fixed.fix: The ';' joining the assignment to the loop becomes '&&'. A simple assignment carries the exit status of its last command substitution, so a failed cd short-circuits the walk instead of entering it with an empty p. concerns.site: the nine-copy block, 'Where to put it' paragraph, all 9 of plugins/pipeline/agents/*.md
concerns.property: Every worked location example in the block is true on the machine that authored it and stated unconditionally. The block says: 'a tree under a mode-700 ancestor, or under `$TMPDIR`, PASSES.' `$TMPDIR` is 0700 on this macOS box. Where TMPDIR is unset - the POSIX default, and the common case on Linux hosts and in containers - `$TMPDIR` expands to nothing or to /tmp, which is mode 1777. The sentence then names, as a worked PASSING example, the exact world-traversable location the same block's live counter-example REFUSES.
concerns.observation: `stat -f %Lp $TMPDIR` = 700 here; `/private/tmp` = 777. Re-running the battery with `TMPDIR=/tmp` (the unset-TMPDIR shape) flips AC16.tmpd from PASS to FAIL: 'expected ADMIT, got REFUSE(every ancestor grants o+x and the leaf is other-accessible)'. So the shipped example AND the cell that blesses it are both properties of the runner, not of the rule. My Phase-3a reference implementation could not have exposed this: I built and ran it on this same box. The same shape, weaker direction, applies to '~/.cache/<name> FAILS it' - true only because $HOME is 755 here; on a distro with a 0700 home it is false in the safe (over-refusing) direction, so I am not blocking on that half.
concerns.must_satisfy: The `$TMPDIR` example is removed, or made conditional on a check the reader runs ('$TMPDIR PASSES where it is 0700, as on macOS; where TMPDIR is unset it falls back to a world-traversable /tmp and FAILS - stat it, do not assume'). AND AC16.tmpd stops asserting an unconditional ADMIT: it must first read $TMPDIR's mode and state the expected verdict as a function of it, so a Linux run reports 'correct, and $TMPDIR is 1777 here' instead of a red cell that looks like a broken harness.

concerns.property: RULING ON THE LIVE-DEFECT CONTROL. Anchoring a control on a live defect is legitimate as EVIDENCE and illegitimate as a MANDATORY cell, because the correct resolution of the defect breaks the instrument. AC16.live is currently the second kind: it is not merely stale-when-fixed, it is red-when-fixed, and it makes the battery's exit code depend on a world-readable checkout continuing to exist.

Dev naming the expiry in impl-report `made_load_bearing[4]` satisfies the first half of the shelf-life rule; the second half is missing, because the expiry sentence is not where the next reader meets the failure. And the panel instruction to leave the registry at 18 means this round is being asked to preserve a live leak so a fixture keeps working, which is the coupling itself.
concerns.must_satisfy: AC16.live's ABSENCE becomes a PASS whose message states the expiry in place ('the live counter-example is gone, which is the correct outcome; the world-traversable-checkout class is still covered by AC16.bare - re-anchor only if live evidence is wanted'), and the load-bearing discrimination moves to AC16.bare.
